note: Re-judged 2026-11-20 by an independent agent after 47f7ca7b55 gave the row a {partial} annotation; no tagged unit changed, and enforced cannot stand under a partial. RFC 4301 Section 7.3: "Also, the receiver MUST discard non-initial fragments that do not comply with the security policy applied to the overall packet." Tested: "discard non-initial fragments that do not comply with the security policy applied to the overall packet". Gap: "the receiver". Producer: internal/component/ike/engine/child.go::installChildDataplane. The packet tests TestRFC4301FragmentsOfACompliantPacketAreDelivered and TestRFC4301FragmentsOfANonCompliantPacketAreDiscarded (revert records on appendChildPolicies) send the non-initial fragment before the initial one, each in its own ESP packet on a tunnel-mode SA delivering to this node: the compliant inner packet is reassembled and delivered with XfrmInNoPols unchanged, the outside-source one is not delivered and moves XfrmInStateMismatch by exactly one. They grant fragment permission through fragmentPermittedChild, so the selector check and not a missing permission makes the discard. The boundary units pin the inbound selector and template and refuse a widened selector or a templated bypass. The gateway receiver, where Ze forwards the decapsulated packet and FWD is checked after K3 gathers it, has no tagged test, as the annotation says. Scoped evidence only; zero whole-requirement credit.
